newsitem.title: UK: LME copper gives back some more gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper gives back some more gains in late trade.

text.p: Profit taking eroded some of the gains on the London Metal Exchange's copper contract during Tuesday's late trading and tin levelled out after higher prices proved unsustainable earlier, dealers said.
At 1800 GMT copper was available at $2,410/2,413 about $6.00 under the kerb close while tin held on to unchanged levels from the last ring at $5,730/$5,735.

Three months copper skipped to $2,433 per tonne in earlier inter-office trade after hectic activity on the morning kerb, the highest since early March. Widespread buying was seen, including by funds, traders said
But once ring trading resumed in the afternoon, producer selling and profit-taking eroded the gains, and prices ended the afternoon kerb only $8 higher at $2,417.
"Fundamentally it still looks good, but I think it may need to build a base above $2,400," said analyst Helen Williamson of broker Brandeis.
The next major target is $2,440, the high of March 7.
The other metals were barely changed in generally sparse business.
